dedupe_keys.name: invest integrated valuation of ecosystem services and tradeoffs

description: InVEST is a suite of more than twenty free, open-source software models for mapping and valuing the goods and services that nature provides, developed by the Natural Capital Alliance at Stanford University (formerly the Natural Capital Project). It includes ecosystem service models for terrestrial, freshwater, marine and coastal ecosystems and urban settings, for example coastal vulnerability and habitat protection, urban flood risk mitigation, urban cooling, stormwater retention, sediment and nutrient delivery, water yield and carbon storage. Models are run from the InVEST Workbench desktop application or as the natcap.invest Python package (version 3.20.2, September 2026, Apache-2.0), and a plugin registry lets the community add models and workflows; a Data Hub offers global layers and pre-processed inputs. Everything is free of charge. Caveats: the models are deliberately simple, spatially explicit production functions whose results depend on local parameters, they give relative, not engineering-grade estimates, and valuation assumptions need care. It is used to quantify how green and blue infrastructure such as mangroves, wetlands, urban trees and floodplains reduces hazard exposure and supports climate adaptation, and to compare nature-based and grey options; it consumes land cover such as ESA WorldCover and relates to i-Tree for urban trees.
inputs: land use and land cover rasters
